per-line Tweedie training power, since the 1.5→1.3→1.1 sweep (results.tsv ec0919f/db986b2/e65d47a) kept raising motor and contents but buildings' B-fold D² fell from 0.09728 at power 1.3 to 0.09608 at power 1.1 — the lines don't share an op

Stronger regularization (backlog item 2, K9) — with only ~7% of rows carrying claims, 31-leaf trees at min_data_in_leaf 500 likely overfit noise in small leaves, which is where fold A (the weaker fold for motor and contents) loses the most

Cap motor's training rate target before fitting (backlog item 4, J2/J3) — the unlimited UK third-party bodily-injury cover produces one 11.9m claim that dominates motor's Tweedie deviance and likely distorts tree splits.

owner decision (Karl): monotone constraints on excess, NCB, licence points, flood zone, prior claims; score-neutral, adopted for defensible and portable relativities

Backlog 1.2 — float buildings' weather-peril component (storm, flood, subsidence) on its own model instead of anchoring it, since ae_buildings_B has been pinned at 1.049 across every prior kept run because anchoring discards the 2025 weathe

Backlog 1.1 — split motor into a Poisson frequency model for bodily injury (count-based, immune to the single 11.9m claim distorting cost splits) plus severity supplied only by anchoring, with other motor perils left on the original Tweedie

Anchor each line's level using only the two most recent on-levelled training years instead of the full training window, per backlog item 1.3, since portfolio mix drift makes older years less representative of the valid year's mix.
sample_weight = exposure × completion from comp_* columns, so immature (low-completion) rows' noisier y_ult estimate counts less (backlog 1.4, Tier 1, untried).

backlog 2.1 — out-of-fold credibility (target) encoding for high-cardinality categoricals (e.g. make_model, occupation, previous_insurer) should beat LightGBM's native categorical splits, since thousands of levels need shrinkage toward the

Backlog item 2.2 — engineered peril-mechanics interaction features (subsidence, escape-of-water, flood) should let the GBM find risk combinations that shallow, heavily-regularized trees (num_leaves 15, min_data_in_leaf 2000) are unlikely to

credibility encoding is fit once per line on the combined cost rate and reused by both motor sub-models, reintroducing the 11.9m BI claim into the "other" peril model's encodings — exactly what backlog 1.1's BI/other split was meant to keep

backlog 2.3 — isotonic recalibration of each Tweedie sub-rate (buildings, contents, motor's non-BI perils) from an inner time-holdout should correct systematic under/over-prediction at the tails that min_data_in_leaf=2000 trees can't fully

Motor BI frequency sub-model is misspecified — it fits raw claim count weighted by exposure instead of count/exposure weighted by exposure, so exposure's effect on frequency is left unmodelled and then double-applied at `pred = rate * expos
SMOKE CRASH (): CANN-lite (backlog 2.4) — a GLM linear predictor as LightGBM init_score should let smooth main effects beat what 15-leaf trees approximate coarsely.

Backlog 2.9 — normalize `written_premium` by each row's own line-year mean, since the raw level drifts year to year with rate changes and a model trained on 2021-23 premiums under/over-shoots fold B's 2024 (or 2025 test) premium range.

Widen the seed bag from 3 to 8 seeds with feature/bagging fraction varied per seed (0.7/0.8/0.9 cycling), per backlog item 2.5, since single-seed noise (sd 0.0026) is close to the gains most hypotheses have produced this batch.
